slides.title: CFD foundations — FV, spectral, lattice-Boltzmann, IB
slides.body:
**Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)**: numerical solution of fluid PDEs. Industry workhorse since 1980s. Founders: **Frank Harlow** (LANL, MAC method), **Suhas Patankar** (SIMPLE algorithm), **Peyret + Roache** (V&V), **Brian Spalding** (PHOENICS first commercial code).

**Discretization methods**:

**1. Finite Volume (FV)** — most widespread. Integrate conservation laws over control volumes; ensures exact local conservation. Fluxes computed at cell faces via Riemann solvers (Roe, HLL, HLLC, AUSM). Used by ANSYS Fluent, OpenFOAM, Star-CCM+, SU2. Handles complex geometries + general meshes well. Standard for industrial aerodynamics, combustion, turbomachinery, automotive.

**2. Finite Difference (FD)** — replace derivatives with difference quotients. Simple, works on structured grids. Used in atmospheric + oceanic models + many academic codes. Less flexible than FV for complex geometry.

**3. Finite Element (FE)** — weak formulation + basis functions. Strong in solid mechanics + multiphysics; less common in compressible flow but used heavily in incompressible CFD (FEniCS, Nektar++) + biomedical.

**4. Spectral methods** — Fourier or Chebyshev basis; exponential convergence for smooth solutions. Best for canonical flows (channel DNS, isotropic turbulence) on simple geometries. **Kim, Moin, Moser** classic channel-DNS code uses spectral.

**5. Spectral element / Discontinuous Galerkin (DG)** — combines geometric flexibility of FE with spectral accuracy. Codes: Nek5000, NekRS, FLEXI, FlowPM. Hot area for exascale.

**6. Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM)** — instead of solving NS directly, evolve a discrete-velocity Boltzmann equation on a lattice. Macroscopic NS recovered in continuum limit. Highly parallel, ideal for porous media + complex geometry + multiphase. Codes: Palabos, OpenLB, M-Star CFD, NVIDIA Modulus' LBM modules.

**7. Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH)** — meshless Lagrangian particles. Free surfaces, splashing, astrophysics. **Gingold + Monaghan + Lucy** (1977). Codes: DualSPHysics, splatNs.

**8. Immersed Boundary (IB) methods** — solve flow on a fixed Cartesian grid + add forcing terms to enforce no-slip on arbitrary moving bodies. Avoids re-meshing for moving / deforming geometries (insects, fish, heart valves). **Peskin** (1972, heart valve simulation), **Mittal**, **Verzicco**.

**Time integration**: explicit Runge-Kutta (compressible), semi-implicit fractional-step or projection methods (incompressible — Chorin 1968, Temam 1969). For stiff problems IMEX schemes or fully implicit BDF.

**Linear solvers** (incompressible pressure-Poisson dominates cost): conjugate gradient, GMRES, multigrid (algebraic + geometric), preconditioned Krylov. Modern: hypre, PETSc, AmgX.

**Languages + frameworks**: Fortran (legacy + HPC), C/C++ (OpenFOAM, SU2), Python wrappers + JAX/PyTorch for differentiable CFD (JAX-CFD, PhiFlow, NVIDIA Modulus, Lettuce LBM-PyTorch).

slides.title: Meshes, adaptivity + verification & validation (V&V)
slides.body:
**Mesh generation** is often the rate-limiting step in industrial CFD (~60-80% of engineer time).

**Mesh types**:
- **Structured (hexahedral)** — logical i,j,k indexing; efficient + accurate but rigid for complex shapes. Aerodynamic wings, turbomachinery cascades.
- **Unstructured (tetra/poly)** — flexible; meshes arbitrary geometry. Most automotive + ship + biomedical CFD. Hex-dominated polyhedral cells (Pointwise, Star-CCM+ poly) improve accuracy.
- **Overset (chimera)** — overlapping component grids interpolate across boundaries; used for moving bodies (helicopter blades, store separation).
- **Cartesian + cut-cell** — Cartesian grid + special cells at boundaries. Easy auto-meshing; popular in academic + open-source codes + lattice-Boltzmann.
- **Body-fitted** — clusters cells near walls to resolve boundary layers.

**Y+ requirement**: first-cell y+ < 1 for wall-resolved (no wall function), y+ ~ 30-300 for wall-functions. RANS quality + LES near-wall resolution depend strongly on this.

**Mesh adaptive refinement (AMR)**: refine cells where solution gradients are largest (shocks, shear layers, vortices). **Berger + Oliger** (1984), **Berger + Colella** (1989). Used in shock-dominated + multiphase flows (PARAMESH, Chombo, BoxLib, AMReX). Saves orders of magnitude in DOF vs uniform.

**Grid convergence + Richardson extrapolation**: solve on grids h, h/2, h/4; estimate solution + order of convergence + extrapolated value. **Grid Convergence Index (GCI)** (Roache 1994) is the standard quantitative measure.

**Verification + Validation (V&V)** — formalized by **Pat Roache** + **Bill Oberkampf**:
- **Verification**: 'are you solving the equations right?' Compare to analytic solutions (manufactured solutions, MMS), check grid convergence + iterative residuals.
- **Validation**: 'are you solving the right equations?' Compare to experiments + DNS benchmarks.
- **Uncertainty quantification (UQ)**: propagate uncertainties in inputs + models to outputs. **AIAA G-077** + **ASME V&V20** are industry standards.

**Famous benchmark cases**:
- **Backward-facing step** (separation + reattachment).
- **NACA 0012 airfoil** at various Re, α.
- **Turbulent channel flow** (Moser-Kim-Mansour DNS).
- **Flow over a cylinder** (Bénard-Kármán shedding, drag crisis).
- **DLR-F6 + Common Research Model** (transonic transport aero).
- **Ahmed body** (automotive bluff aero).
- **HiFiLES NASA Juncture Flow** (corner separation).
- **AIAA Drag Prediction Workshop** + Turbulence Modeling Resource.

**Verification + validation are non-negotiable**: a CFD prediction without quantified error bars is useless for safety-critical design (aircraft, nuclear, medical devices). FAA + EASA require V&V documentation for certification.

slides.title: Modern frontier — GPUs, neural surrogates, bio-inspired
slides.body:
**Hardware revolution**:
- **GPU CFD**: 10-100× speedup over CPU. NVIDIA Modulus, M-Star CFD, NVIDIA Simulation, Altair nanoFluidX use GPUs natively. AMD MI300X + Intel Ponte Vecchio + custom ASICs (Cerebras CS-3 for CFD) emerging.
- **Exascale supercomputers**: Frontier (1.1 EFLOP/s, Oak Ridge), Aurora (Argonne), El Capitan (LLNL). DNS now possible at Re_τ ~ 5000 channel, Re_λ ~ 1300 isotropic. Realistic-aircraft LES becoming routine.
- **Cloud CFD**: AWS Parallel Cluster, Azure HPC, Rescale, Simscale — democratized access.

**Machine learning + neural surrogates**:
- **Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs)** (Raissi + Karniadakis 2019): train neural networks whose loss includes PDE residuals + boundary conditions. Solve forward + inverse problems with sparse data. Works well for low-dimensional + smooth PDEs; struggles with stiffness + multi-scale turbulence.
- **Fourier Neural Operators (FNO)** (Li + Anandkumar 2020): learn solution operators in spectral space; generalize across resolutions; orders-of-magnitude faster than CFD for inference.
- **Graph Neural Networks for fluids** (Pfaff + Battaglia, DeepMind MeshGraphNets 2020): mesh-based ML predictions of unsteady flow.
- **Neural-network turbulence closures** (Ling, Templeton, Duraisamy, Brunton, Kutz, Maulik, Moin's group): tensor-basis NN, SINDy, RL-driven RANS / LES.
- **AlphaFold-style for fluids**: **AlphaFlow** (DeepMind/Imperial College 2024) for transient turbulent flow prediction. **Neural ODE-based** + **diffusion-based** generative simulators.
- **NVIDIA Modulus**: open-source AI-physics framework — PINNs, FNOs, hybrid solvers. Used by Siemens, BMW, Lockheed.
- **ECMWF GraphCast + Aurora + FengWu** (DeepMind, Microsoft, Shanghai AI Lab) for weather: equivalent of NS for atmosphere + ocean; 10000× faster than traditional NWP; comparable accuracy. Pure data-driven Earth-system models a major frontier.

**Differentiable CFD**: PDE solvers that propagate gradients backward through time + space, enabling end-to-end optimization (JAX-CFD, PhiFlow, Φ-Flow, Diff-FoamFlow). Use cases: shape optimization, control, inverse design, calibrating turbulence models from data.

**Bio-inspired + animal-inspired fluid mechanics**:
- **Jellyfish propulsion**: ultra-efficient — pulsed-jet + suction. Inspires AUV designs (Costello, Dabiri, Colin).
- **Fish + schooling**: Strouhal St ≈ 0.25-0.35 for cruising — universal swimming optimum. Phalanx + diamond schooling formations exploit vortex wakes for energetic gain.
- **Insect flight + clap-and-fling** (Weis-Fogh 1973): hovering hawkmoths + butterflies use vortex lift; **MAV** (micro-air-vehicle) design (Wood lab Harvard RoboBee, DelFly).
- **Bird flight + V-formation**: trailing birds exploit upwash from leaders; 15-20% energy savings.
- **Whale fin + bumps (tubercles)** — humpback flipper tubercles delay stall + reduce drag. **Tubercle-inspired wind-turbine blades** (WhalePower).
- **Shark skin + riblets**: micro-grooves reduce turbulent skin friction ~5%. Used in 3M films + Boeing fuselage trials.
- **Sailfish + tuna**: rigid leading edge + caudal-fin oscillation; high-frequency thrust at Strouhal optimum.
- **Cephalopod jet propulsion** — variable-area nozzle adaptive jets.

**Industrial + societal applications**:
- **Aviation**: 787 + A350 + F-35 entirely CFD-driven aero + propulsion design.
- **Automotive**: F1 + EVs + autonomous-driving cooling, all CFD.
- **Climate + weather**: GCMs (ECMWF IFS, NOAA GFS, UKMO Unified Model); ML hybrid emerging (GraphCast, Aurora).
- **Energy**: wind farms, hydropower, fusion (tokamak edge), oil recovery.
- **Biomedical**: cardiovascular surgery planning, drug delivery, prosthetic-valve design.
- **Drug discovery**: protein-protein hydrodynamics, AI-fluids for organ-on-chip.
- **Hypersonics + space**: Starship, Skylon, Hermeus, NASA hypersonics + plasma propulsion.

The future of fluid mechanics: **GPU-accelerated + differentiable + ML-augmented + bio-inspired** CFD, working at exascale + integrating into automated design pipelines. The Navier-Stokes equations themselves remain unsolved analytically (Clay Prize), but our practical mastery over them grows year by year.

question.question: Estimate DNS cost for an aircraft wing
question.goal: Aircraft wing chord c = 3 m, U = 250 m/s, ν = 1.5·10⁻⁵. Estimate Re_c, Kolmogorov scale η, total DNS DOF in 3D, + total operation count for one flow-through time.

steps.prompt: Estimate η/c using K41 scaling η/L ~ Re^{−3/4}.
steps.reveal: (5·10⁷)^{0.75} ≈ 1.9·10⁶. So η/c ~ 5·10⁻⁷; η ~ 1.6 μm. Boundary-layer Kolmogorov scale even smaller near the wall.

steps.prompt: Estimate 3D mesh DOF assuming uniform η-resolution.

acceptedAnswers: DOF ~ (c/η)³ ~ (5·10⁶)³ wait. Uniform DOF (c/η)³ ~ (2·10⁶)³ = 8·10¹⁸; for boundary-layer-relevant volume smaller.

steps.reveal: DOF ~ (L/η)³ ~ Re^{9/4} ~ (5·10⁷)^{9/4} ~ 5·10¹⁶ for uniform mesh — astronomical. In practice the boundary layer is the dominant subdomain + DOF for wall-resolved DNS in a turbulent boundary layer scale as Re^{2.7} or so for the BL + Re² for wall-modeled LES (Choi + Moin 2012).

acceptedAnswers: Even at exascale full aircraft DNS would take years; out of reach. Wall-modeled LES at Re^{~1} is feasible.

hints: 1 FLOP per DOF per time step; many time steps.
steps.reveal: Each time step needs ~100 FLOP/DOF + we need many flow-through times (~10⁵-10⁶ steps). Total ~5·10¹⁶ × 100 × 10⁵ ~ 5·10²³ FLOP. At Frontier (~10¹⁸ FLOP/s) ~ 5·10⁵ s ~ 6 days per simulation, **assuming perfect scaling on a uniform mesh — never achievable**. Realistic estimates give years per case. Hence wall-modeled LES (cost ~ Re or Re¹·⁵) + hybrid RANS-LES + ML closures are the engineering path forward; DNS reserved for low-Re research + canonical validation.

question.question: Why are PINNs, FNOs + ML-augmented CFD considered a frontier rather than yet a replacement for traditional solvers?
options: **PINNs (Raissi-Karniadakis 2019)** + **Fourier Neural Operators (Li-Anandkumar 2020)** + graph-neural-network solvers can be **orders of magnitude faster** for inference + naturally differentiable for inverse / optimization problems. But they have **limitations**: (1) **generalization** — trained on a flow class, may fail outside it (compared to NS, which works everywhere); (2) **stiffness + multi-scale** turbulence remains hard; (3) **uncertainty quantification** + **out-of-distribution** detection are immature; (4) **convergence + stability guarantees** are weaker than for traditional FV / FE methods with formal proofs; (5) **certification + V&V** infrastructure (FAA, ASME) does not yet accept ML predictions for safety-critical design. So they currently augment rather than replace: ML closures inside RANS / LES (Ling, Duraisamy, Maulik), neural surrogates for design-space exploration, differentiable CFD for inverse design (JAX-CFD, PhiFlow). Tools like NVIDIA Modulus + Boltz / AlphaFlow / AlphaFold-style models suggest a long-term trajectory toward AI-native physical simulation, but the path is empirical + ongoing.
question.explanation: PINNs + FNOs + GNN-based CFD are very fast + naturally differentiable. But generalization, stiffness, multi-scale turbulence, UQ, OOD detection + certification (FAA, ASME V&V) are immature. They currently augment classical CFD (ML closures, design exploration, inverse design) rather than replace it. Long-term trajectory is AI-native physics simulation.

slides.workedSolution: ML surrogates (PINNs, FNOs, GNNs) are fast + differentiable, ideal for inverse design. But generalization, multi-scale turbulence, UQ + certification (FAA, ASME V&V) are immature. Currently augment classical CFD (ML closures, design exploration). Path toward AI-native simulation is empirical + ongoing.

question.question: ML-augmented CFD project plan
question.prompt: You lead aerodynamics at a startup designing a novel eVTOL aircraft. Outline a CFD workflow combining (a) traditional RANS / LES on GPU clusters, (b) ML turbulence closures trained on DNS / LES libraries, (c) FNO / PINN surrogate models for design-space exploration, (d) experimental validation in wind tunnel. Discuss V&V documentation needed for FAA certification + how you'd manage uncertainty quantification + out-of-distribution risk.

question.question: Write the Strouhal number St for an oscillating fish-tail of frequency f, amplitude A, swimming speed U (canonical biological cruising form).

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why modern CFD is being transformed by GPUs, ML + bio-inspired design.
question.rubric: Mentions: traditional CFD (FV / FE / spectral / LBM) on CPUs is mature but expensive — full-aircraft LES at Re ~ 10⁷ still pushes exascale limits. Three concurrent revolutions: (1) **GPU + exascale hardware** (Frontier, Aurora, El Capitan; NVIDIA Modulus, AMD MI300X) gives 10-100× speedup + enables routine LES + DNS for canonical cases. (2) **ML + neural surrogates** — PINNs (Raissi-Karniadakis 2019), FNOs (Li-Anandkumar 2020), graph-NN solvers (DeepMind MeshGraphNets), Reynolds-stress ML closures (Ling, Duraisamy, Maulik, Brunton-Kutz), AlphaFlow + differentiable CFD frameworks (JAX-CFD, PhiFlow) accelerate inference + enable inverse design. (3) **Bio-inspired design** — jellyfish propulsion, fish schooling Strouhal optimum, insect clap-and-fling, whale tubercles, shark riblets inform AUVs, drones, wind turbines, swimsuits. Concludes: Navier-Stokes remains analytically unsolved (Clay Prize) but our practical mastery — driven by GPU + ML + biology + classical theory — grows year by year, transforming aviation, automotive, energy, biomedical + climate science.
